cells.tense: Both hands are on what you're responsible for, and nothing in you is straining to hold it.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you're letting end and what you're tending in its place, and let them hear it. That's the release that finishing gives, said out loud where it counts.
cells.core:
You can look at what needs to end and let it end without flinching, and you can tend what's already growing without hovering over it. When one demand is heavy and the other needs you, you hold both and you don't lose track of which is which. That steadiness is why the endings don't tear anything loose.

Name what you're letting go of, and name what you're tending now, to one person who can hear it. What it gives you is the willingness to let the next ending come when it's time, because you'll know the clearing is part of the planting. The cost is that saying it out loud means someone can ask you later how it went.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what's yours and letting what's done be done.
cells.place: on ground that's already been cleared and is waiting for something to be planted

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead there's a version of this where the clearing is finally finished and you can rest, and you're already living in it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been carrying past its time and put it down today, unfinished if that's how it has to go. The satisfaction of seeing something through comes once you stop trying to hold it where it was.
cells.core:
There's a picture of what this is supposed to look like when it's done, and that picture is running the show. You're holding every piece of what's left as though letting any of it go before the whole thing is finished would undo the work. But the clearing you're bracing against has already happened in every way that matters, and no amount of holding it forward changes that.

On a good day, you decide what's over and you let it be over, and the deciding is quick because you're not waiting for a feeling of readiness that hasn't arrived. Pick one piece of what you're still managing — one item on a list, one thing in a room, one unfinished obligation — and let it be finished today. What that gives you is the deep satisfaction of actually being where you are, given how much of your life is spent trying to be there ahead of time.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the ending open past the point where it was already done.
cells.place: on ground that's already been cleared and is waiting for something to be planted

cells.tense: You're still standing at a doorway you already walked through, and your hands haven't caught up to the fact that the room behind you is empty.
cells.ask: Put one thing in a drawer today, all the way in, and close it. Not a decision, just a drawer. Finishing something small can put strength back in you for the endings you haven't started.
cells.core:
There was a clearing you were supposed to finish, and it stopped partway. What was meant to be gone is still being carried, on top of everything else. On a good day, you notice when something is over and you let it be over and you move your attention to what's next, without needing a reason or a ceremony.

That act isn't beyond you. It just hasn't happened yet. Pick one small thing, the kind that sits around because closing it seems like more than it is, and finish it today. Not the whole cupboard, one thing. You can admit it's just one thing, and that's enough. Finishing it is how the strength comes back, when you're not sure it will.
cells.sheetLine: You were supposed to finish letting something go, and you stopped halfway.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but the page keeps getting written anyway, because you're still tending what's around you without calling it that.
cells.ask: Tell someone what you've been holding on to and why, in your own words. The acknowledgment you're owed for holding it can reach you once you've said it's yours.
cells.core:
You're doing the work of deciding what stays and what goes, and you're doing it quietly, and you'd probably tell anyone who asked that you're not deciding anything. But you are. Letting something be finished instead of reviving it, or keeping something running because it's yours to keep running, is a choice you're making. On a good day, you know what you've handed over and what you've held, and you can say so without making it a performance.

The easier version of this is the one where you let someone know what you did. Not a summary, the specific thing. That's what's missing here, not the work itself, which is already underway. Choose one ending you've been part of and tell the person closest to it what it cost you to be there for it. Having that seen for what it was changes what it means to you. It doesn't make the next ending easier, but it makes it yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're doing the clearing. You just haven't claimed the doing.
